## What this project is and how it flows

This is a local bank simulation for studying replay defenses. A signed transaction passes through authentication/session binding and then the configured check order. HMAC verification is implemented in `server/utils/hmac.js` and invoked in `server/core.js`; timestamp bounds use `server/utils/timestamp.js`; nonce consumption is in `server/utils/nonce.js`; request-ID lookup is in `server/utils/idempotency.js`; balance and ledger writes are in `server/core.js`. `CHECK_ORDER` is parsed near the top of `server/core.js` and the pipeline dispatches those checks before the balance transaction. `IDEMPOTENCY_POLICY=success_only` permits a fresh retry after a FAILED insufficient-balance row while blocking duplicate successful IDs; `any_outcome` treats either SUCCESS or FAILED as consumed. In both policies callers should retry an insufficient balance only after funding and with a fresh nonce; using a new request ID is required under `any_outcome`.

## Plain-English request flow

This is a local bank simulation for studying replay defenses. A signed transaction passes through authentication/session binding and then the configured check order. HMAC verification is implemented in `server/utils/hmac.js` and invoked in `server/core.js`; timestamp bounds use `server/utils/timestamp.js`; nonce consumption is in `server/utils/nonce.js`; request-ID lookup is in `server/utils/idempotency.js`; balance and ledger writes are in `server/core.js`. `CHECK_ORDER` is parsed near the top of `server/core.js` and the pipeline dispatches those checks before the balance transaction. `IDEMPOTENCY_POLICY=success_only` permits a fresh retry after a FAILED insufficient-balance row while blocking duplicate successful IDs; `any_outcome` treats either SUCCESS or FAILED as consumed. In both policies callers should retry an insufficient balance only after funding and with a fresh nonce; using a new request ID is required under `any_outcome`.

### HTTP routes

| Method | Path | Authentication / checks | Gate |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/health` | none | none |
| POST | `/api/login` | user ID and PIN; issues bearer session | none |
| GET | `/api/balance/:user_id` | bearer session bound to user | none |
| GET | `/api/transactions/:user_id` | bearer session bound to user | none |
| POST | `/api/deposit` | bearer, signed-request pipeline, account ownership | deposit replay protection / defense flags |
| POST | `/api/withdraw` | bearer, signed-request pipeline, account ownership and balance | defense flags |
| POST | `/api/reset` | demo-only reset operation | `ENABLE_DEMO_ROUTES` |
| POST | `/api/demo/nonce-crash` | demo nonce wipe operation | `ENABLE_DEMO_ROUTES` |
| POST | `/__test/fault/nonce-store` | test-only fault injection | `ENABLE_TEST_FAULT_ROUTE` |
| GET | `/__test/unhandled-error` | test-only error path | `ENABLE_TEST_FAULT_ROUTE` |
| POST | `/__test/profile/flush` | test-only profiling flush | `ENABLE_TEST_FAULT_ROUTE` |

### SQLite schema and indexes

Initialization and migration SQL excerpt from server/core.js; full source and migration tests follow.

```js
  if (!/request_id\s+TEXT\s+UNIQUE/i.test(table.sql || '')) return;
  await run('BEGIN IMMEDIATE');
  try {
    await run('ALTER TABLE transactions RENAME TO transactions_legacy');
    await run(`CREATE TABLE transactions (
      id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
      request_id TEXT NOT NULL,
      user_id TEXT NOT NULL,
      account_id TEXT NOT NULL,
      type TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(type IN ('DEPOSIT', 'WITHDRAW')),
      amount INTEGER NOT NULL,
      currency TEXT DEFAULT 'BDT',
      status TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(status IN ('SUCCESS', 'FAILED')),
      reason TEXT,
      signature TEXT,
      created_at DATETIME DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
      FOREIGN KEY (user_id) REFERENCES accounts(user_id)
    )`);
    await run(`INSERT INTO transactions (id, request_id, user_id, account_id, type, amount, currency, status, reason, signature, created_at)
      SELECT id, request_id, user_id, account_id, type, amount, currency, status, reason, signature, created_at FROM transactions_legacy`);
    await run('DROP TABLE transactions_legacy');
    await run('COMMIT');
  } catch (error) {
    await run('ROLLBACK').catch(() => {});
    throw error;
  }
}

async function initializeDatabase() {
  await run('PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL');
  await run('PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON');
  await run(`CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS accounts (
    user_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, username TEXT NOT NULL, balance INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 10000,
    currency TEXT DEFAULT 'BDT', account_id TEXT, pin_salt TEXT, pin_hash TEXT,
    created_at DATETIME DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
  )`);
  for (const [column, type] of [['account_id', 'TEXT'], ['pin_salt', 'TEXT'], ['pin_hash', 'TEXT']]) {
    if (!(await hasColumn('accounts', column))) await run(`ALTER TABLE accounts ADD COLUMN ${column} ${type}`);
  }
  await run(`CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS transactions (
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, request_id TEXT NOT NULL, user_id TEXT NOT NULL,
    account_id TEXT NOT NULL, type TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(type IN ('DEPOSIT', 'WITHDRAW')),
    amount INTEGER NOT NULL, currency TEXT DEFAULT 'BDT', status TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(status IN ('SUCCESS', 'FAILED')),
    reason TEXT, signature TEXT, created_at DATETIME DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    FOREIGN KEY (user_id) REFERENCES accounts(user_id)
  )`);
  await migrateTransactions();
  await run('DROP INDEX IF EXISTS idx_transactions_success_request_id');
  await run('DROP INDEX IF EXISTS idx_transactions_any_outcome_request_id');
  if (DEFENSES.request_id && IDEMPOTENCY_POLICY === 'any_outcome') {
    await run("CREATE UNIQUE INDEX idx_transactions_any_outcome_request_id ON transactions(request_id) WHERE status IN ('SUCCESS', 'FAILED')");
  } else if (DEFENSES.request_id) {
    await run("CREATE UNIQUE INDEX idx_transactions_success_request_id ON transactions(request_id) WHERE status = 'SUCCESS'");
  }
  await run(`CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS used_nonces (
    user_id TEXT NOT NULL, nonce TEXT NOT NULL, expires_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY(user_id, nonce)
  )`);
  await run('CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_used_nonces_expires_at ON used_nonces(expires_at)');
  if (NONCE_BACKEND === 'memory' || NONCE_BACKEND === 'sqlite') {
    if (nonceSweepTimer) clearInterval(nonceSweepTimer);
    nonceSweepTimer = startNonceSweep({ backend: NONCE_BACKEND, store: NONCE_BACKEND === 'memory' ? memoryNonces : db, now: () => now() });
  }
```

+# Claims and Evidence
+
+This is an evidence map, not a claim that each result generalizes beyond the local simulation. Row IDs refer to `PAPER_FACTS_CURATED.md`. Confidence intervals and measurement scope are preserved there and in the cited raw files.
+
+| Candidate claim | Supporting curated fact rows | Evidence sufficient? | Caveats |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| 1. Each of the four REST layers is necessary (leave-one-out). | `E1/H1T1N1R1/*/debit`; compare to the corresponding leave-one-out configs `H0T1N1R1`, `H1T0N1R1`, `H1T1N0R1`, and `H1T1N1R0`; token-only evidence `E1/H*/S11/debit`. | **Limited, for the tested scenarios only.** The 16-cell ablation identifies cases where removing one layer changes an outcome. | Thirty attempts per ordinary scenario, deterministic local traffic, single Node process, and synthetic attack model. E1 is not a proof that every layer is necessary for every deployment or attacker. “None” still retains bearer authentication and ownership checks. |
+| 2. Idempotency alone is insufficient against a replay of a previously failed request; policy trade-off. | E1 `S10_fast`/`S10_late` rows for `R1`; C2 rows `C2 success_only H1T1N1R1 S10_fast`, `... S10_late`, and `C2 any_outcome H1T1N1R1 ...`; resubmission variants `same_request_id_fresh_nonce` and `new_request_id_fresh_nonce`. | **Sufficient for the implemented retry policies and tested request flows.** | The original 30 replay attempts repeat one captured FAILED request. A nonce or timestamp layer may block before the request-ID layer; these outcomes are order dependent. C2 resubmission uses one selected full-defense configuration. |
+| 3. Nonce TTL must be at least PAST + FUTURE. | `E4a H1T1N1R0-TTL4/f0..f2 replay_grid`, `E4a ... TTL6 ...`, `E4a ... TTL8 ...`; `E4a/request-ID-off/ttl-window-rule/violating_cells`. | **Moderate support for the tested time model.** The request-ID-off replay grid had zero rule-violating aggregate cells and the checked outcomes follow the sampled rule. | Scaled profile PAST=6 s, server FUTURE=2 s, offsets 0/1/2 s, and only the listed delays. For TTL4, delays 3 and 5 straddle the TTL boundary; delay 4 itself was not sampled. This supports a configuration rule, not a universal formal proof. |
+| 4. Defense overhead and nonce backend cost. | `E2/*/legitimate/handler_p50_repeat_median`; `C5/all_four|nonce_redis|nonce_sqlite|nonce_memory/*`; `E2/*/reject-cost`. | **Sufficient for relative comparison in this setup.** | Single Windows machine, localhost, Memurai Developer 4.2.3, one Node process. Repeat medians show skew and outliers. Do not present these as production latency estimates. |
+| 5. False rejections are dominated by FUTURE tolerance under the assumed profiles. | All 75 `E3 PAST-* FUTURE-* false-reject` rows plus the assumption rows `E3 P1|P2|P3|assumption|*`. | **Limited.** The sweep provides measured outcomes conditional on three explicit assumptions. | These distributions are assumptions, not empirical network traces. The claim is conditional on the chosen profile parameters, timestamp rule, serialization, and simulator. |
+| 6. Fail-open/fail-closed and lost-response retry behavior. | `E4b fault-fail-open-* replay_availability_Wilson`, `E4b fault-fail-closed-* replay_availability_Wilson`, and all `E4c loss-p*` rows. | **Sufficient for the implemented fault toggle and tested retry patterns.** | Fault injection is an in-process test route. Response loss is simulated by dropping the client-observed first response after the server call, not by packet-level network failure. `NONCE_FAIL` alone does not confirm whether a debit occurred; `ALREADY_PROCESSED` follows the duplicate ID check in the tested order. |
+| 7. Concurrency safety. | `Race|identical-payload|accepted-count-1`; `Race|secret-holder|one-request-id|accepted_and_balance_delta`. | **Moderate for the tested local concurrency cases.** | Repeated 1,000 times at width 50, plus one 50-request shared-ID secret-holder case. This does not establish safety under multi-process deployment, distributed databases, or arbitrary traffic. |
+| 8. Nonce-store state size. | `Memory|accepted|baseline_subtracted_slope`; `Memory|requestid|baseline_subtracted_slope`; `E4d *-rps TTL-* memory`. | **Measured for Memurai 4.2.3 and derived for the table.** | The ~181 B/key slope is a local Memurai measurement. E4d is explicitly a linear extrapolation; it is not a measured deployment footprint. |
+
+## Interpretation limits
+
+- The baseline legitimate request generator holds the signing key. The replay attacker is modeled as a network observer without the key; S9 separately models leaked signing-key capability.
+- The S11 token-only attacker holds a bearer token but lacks the session key. It demonstrates why HMAC cannot be disabled when bearer-only forgery is in scope.
+- No claim here says anything about a real bank, telecom operator, or mobile financial service.
+- Every numeric claim must be tied to the raw artifact path and SHA-256 in `PAPER_FACTS_CURATED.md`.

-### Future timestamp tolerance hypothesis for E3
+### Future timestamp tolerance: E3 measured grid
 
-E3 should sweep future tolerance values of 0 s, 5 s, 30 s, and 60 s and measure false rejections for fast legitimate client clocks. Phase 0 observed rejection at +10 s under the 5 s default. The sweep is a hypothesis to test; no false-rejection rate is claimed yet.

Each of the 75 fresh-server cells sent 2,000 requests; offline rejection recomputation matched every observed decision. These are simulated false-rejection outcomes under stated assumptions, not evidence about any real network. Raw per-request and summary data are indexed under `experiments/results/e3-v2/`, with the compact analysis in `docs/RESULTS_PACK_A.md`.

+### `experiments/e1/finalize-oracle-summary.js`
+
+Bytes: 4058. SHA-256: `5ae55841b02742e8fb6e99b4c9023c1e3284165d037bcae62c8122984f8a5c9d`.

+```js
+const fs = require('fs');
+const path = require('path');
+
+const root = path.resolve(__dirname, '../..');
+const output = path.resolve(process.env.E1_OUTPUT_DIR || path.join(root, 'experiments/results/e1-sqlite-final'));
+const run = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(path.join(output, 'run.json'), 'utf8'));
+const runDirectory = path.join(output, run.dataRunDirectory);
+function parseCsv(text) {
+  const parseLine = (line) => {
+    const values = []; let value = ''; let quoted = false;
+    for (let index = 0; index < line.length; index += 1) {
+      const char = line[index];
+      if (quoted && char === '"' && line[index + 1] === '"') { value += '"'; index += 1; }
+      else if (char === '"') quoted = !quoted;
+      else if (char === ',' && !quoted) { values.push(value); value = ''; }
+      else value += char;
+    }
+    values.push(value); return values;
+  };
+  const lines = text.trimEnd().split(/\r?\n/);
+  const headers = parseLine(lines[0]);
+  return { headers, rows: lines.slice(1).map(parseLine) };
+}
+function writeCsv(file, headers, rows) {
+  const q = (value) => { const s = value === null || value === undefined ? '' : String(value); return /[",\r\n]/.test(s) ? `"${s.replace(/"/g, '""')}"` : s; };
+  fs.writeFileSync(file, `${[headers.join(','), ...rows.map((row) => headers.map((key) => q(row[key])).join(','))].join('\n')}\n`);
+}
+let proxyTimingRows = 0;
+for (const name of fs.readdirSync(runDirectory)) {
+  const directory = path.join(runDirectory, name);
+  if (!fs.statSync(directory).isDirectory()) continue;
+  const stdout = path.join(directory, 'proxy.stdout.log');
+  if (!fs.existsSync(stdout)) continue;
+  const match = fs.readFileSync(stdout, 'utf8').match(/capture file:\s*(.+)/);
+  if (!match) continue;
+  const log = `${match[1].trim()}.jsonl`;
+  if (!fs.existsSync(log)) continue;
+  const timings = fs.readFileSync(log, 'utf8').split(/\r?\n/).filter(Boolean).map((line) => {
+    const item = JSON.parse(line);
+    return { method: item.request.method, path: item.request.path, start_ns: item.start_ns, end_ns: item.end_ns, duration_ns: item.duration_ns, http_status: item.response.statusCode };
+  });
+  if (timings.length) {
+    proxyTimingRows += timings.length;
+    writeCsv(path.join(directory, 'proxy-request-timings.csv'), ['method', 'path', 'start_ns', 'end_ns', 'duration_ns', 'http_status'], timings);
+  }
+}
+const summaryFile = path.join(runDirectory, 'summary.csv');
+const parsed = parseCsv(fs.readFileSync(summaryFile, 'utf8'));
+const rows = parsed.rows.map((cells) => Object.fromEntries(parsed.headers.map((header, index) => [header, cells[index]])));
+for (const row of rows) {
+  if (row.scenario_id === 'LEGITIMATE_CONTROL') continue;
+  row.oracle_integrity_holds = Number(row.oracle_duplicate_debit_count_delta) === 0 && Number(row.oracle_unauthorized_debit_amount_delta) === 0;
+}

+const http = require('http');
+const https = require('https');
+const agents = { 'http:': new http.Agent({ keepAlive: true }), 'https:': new https.Agent({ keepAlive: true }) };
+
+function timedRequest(input, options = {}) {
+  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
+    const url = new URL(input);
+    const start = process.hrtime.bigint();
+    const request = (url.protocol === 'https:' ? https : http).request(url, {
+      method: options.method || 'GET',
+      headers: options.headers || {},
+      agent: agents[url.protocol]
+    }, (response) => {
+      const chunks = [];
+      response.on('data', (chunk) => chunks.push(chunk));
+      response.on('end', () => {
+        const end = process.hrtime.bigint();
+        const text = Buffer.concat(chunks).toString('utf8');
+        let body;
+        try { body = JSON.parse(text); } catch { body = text; }
+        resolve({ start_ns: start.toString(), end_ns: end.toString(), duration_ns: (end - start).toString(), status: response.statusCode, headers: response.headers, body });
+      });
+    });
+    request.on('error', (error) => {
+      const end = process.hrtime.bigint();
+      error.start_ns = start.toString();
+      error.end_ns = end.toString();
+      error.duration_ns = (end - start).toString();
+      reject(error);
+    });
+    if (options.body !== undefined) request.write(options.body);
+    request.end();
+  });

+import csv
+import os
+import sys
+
+import matplotlib
+matplotlib.use('Agg')
+import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
+import numpy as np
+
+root = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
+e1_dir = os.path.join(root, 'experiments', 'results', 'e1-sqlite-final')
+e2_dir = os.path.join(root, 'experiments', 'results', 'e2')
+
+with open(os.path.join(e1_dir, 'summary.csv'), newline='', encoding='utf-8') as f:
+    e1_rows = list(csv.DictReader(f))
+configs = []
+scenarios = [f'S{i}' for i in range(1, 10)]
+for row in e1_rows:
+    if row['scenario_id'] in scenarios and row['config_id'] not in configs:
+        configs.append(row['config_id'])
+matrix = np.full((len(configs), len(scenarios)), np.nan)
+for row in e1_rows:
+    if row['scenario_id'] in scenarios and row['config_id'] in configs and row['attack_success_rate']:
+        matrix[configs.index(row['config_id']), scenarios.index(row['scenario_id'])] = float(row['attack_success_rate'])
+fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(13, max(6, len(configs) * 0.42)), constrained_layout=True)
+image = ax.imshow(matrix, cmap='YlOrRd', vmin=0, vmax=1, aspect='auto')
+ax.set_xticks(range(len(scenarios)), scenarios)
+ax.set_yticks(range(len(configs)), configs)
+ax.set_xlabel('Attack scenario')
+ax.set_ylabel('Defense configuration')
+ax.set_title('E1 attack success rate (SQLite ledger debit count / attempts)')
+for i in range(len(configs)):
+    for j in range(len(scenarios)):
+        value = matrix[i, j]
+        ax.text(j, i, '—' if np.isnan(value) else f'{value:.2f}', ha='center', va='center', fontsize=7, color='black')
+fig.colorbar(image, ax=ax, label='Attack success rate')
+for ext in ('png', 'pdf', 'svg'):
+    fig.savefig(os.path.join(e1_dir, f'attack-success-heatmap.{ext}'), dpi=200)
+plt.close(fig)
+
+with open(os.path.join(e2_dir, 'load-repeat-summary.csv'), newline='', encoding='utf-8') as f:
+    e2_rows = list(csv.DictReader(f))
+stacks = list(dict.fromkeys(row['stack_id'] for row in e2_rows))
+x = np.arange(len(stacks))
+fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(13, 6), constrained_layout=True)
+width = 0.36
+for offset, concurrency in enumerate(('1', '16')):
+    vals, low, high = [], [], []
+    for stack in stacks:
+        row = next((item for item in e2_rows if item['stack_id'] == stack and item['concurrency'] == concurrency), None)
+        vals.append(float(row['mean_repeat_median_ms']) if row else 0)
+        low.append(float(row['mean_repeat_median_ms']) - float(row['ci95_low_ms']) if row else 0)
+        high.append(float(row['ci95_high_ms']) - float(row['mean_repeat_median_ms']) if row else 0)
+    ax.bar(x + (offset - .5) * width, vals, width, yerr=[low, high], capsize=3, label=f'Concurrency {concurrency}')
+ax.set_xticks(x, stacks, rotation=30, ha='right')
+ax.set_ylabel('Mean per-repeat median latency (ms)')
+ax.set_title('E2 end-to-end latency with 95% CI across five repeat medians')
+ax.legend()
+for ext in ('png', 'pdf', 'svg'):
+    fig.savefig(os.path.join(e2_dir, f'latency-by-stack.{ext}'), dpi=200)
+plt.close(fig)
+
+with open(os.path.join(e2_dir, 'load-repeat-summary.csv'), newline='', encoding='utf-8') as f:
+    rows = list(csv.DictReader(f))
+with open(os.path.join(e2_dir, 'load-summary.tex'), 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:
+    f.write('\\begin{tabular}{lrrrrr}\n\\toprule\nStack & C & Mean median (ms) & 95\\% CI low & 95\\% CI high & Repeats \\\\\n\\midrule\n')
+    for row in rows:
+        f.write(f"{row['stack_id']} & {row['concurrency']} & {float(row['mean_repeat_median_ms']):.4f} & {float(row['ci95_low_ms']):.4f} & {float(row['ci95_high_ms']):.4f} & {row['repetitions']} \\\\\n")
+    f.write('\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n')
+
+with open(os.path.join(e2_dir, 'rejection-cost.csv'), newline='', encoding='utf-8') as f:
+    rows = list(csv.DictReader(f))
+with open(os.path.join(e2_dir, 'rejection-cost.tex'), 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:
+    f.write('\\begin{tabular}{llrrrr}\n\\toprule\nOrder & Flood & Attempts & Mean ms & p95 ms & Rejected \\\\\n\\midrule\n')
+    for row in rows:
+        f.write(f"{row['check_order']} & {row['flood']} & {row['attempts']} & {float(row['mean_duration_ms']):.4f} & {float(row['p95_ms']):.4f} & {row['rejected_count']} \\\\\n")
+    f.write('\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n')
+
+print(f'matplotlib {matplotlib.__version__}; wrote E1 heatmap and E2 latency figure in PNG, PDF, SVG plus LaTeX tables')

+        for r in rows:f.write(f"{r['configuration']} & {r['nonce_ttl_seconds']} & {r['client_future_offset_seconds']} & {r['replay_delay_seconds']} & {r['trials']} & {r['accepted']} & {r['blocked']} / \\texttt{{\\detokenize{{{r['blocking_layer_histogram']}}}}} \\\\\n")
+        f.write('\\bottomrule\\end{tabular}\n')
+    if os.path.exists(os.path.join(E4,'e4d-derived.csv')):
+        with open(os.path.join(E4,'e4d-derived.csv'),newline='',encoding='utf-8') as f:derived=list(csv.DictReader(f))
+        with open(os.path.join(E4,'e4d-derived.tex'),'w',encoding='utf-8') as f:
+            f.write('\\begin{tabular}{rrrrrr}\\toprule\nRate & TTL & Derived keys & B/key & Derived bytes & Derived MiB \\\\\n\\midrule\n')
+            for r in derived:f.write(f"{r['requests_per_second']} & {r['ttl_seconds']} & {r['derived_keys']} & {float(r['derived_mean_bytes_per_key']):.5f} & {float(r['derived_memory_bytes']):.0f} & {float(r['derived_memory_mib']):.3f} \\\\\n")
+            f.write('\\bottomrule\\end{tabular}\n')
+    if os.path.exists(os.path.join(E4,'e4b.csv')):
+        rows=read(os.path.join(E4,'e4b.csv'))
+        with open(os.path.join(E4,'fault-mode.tex'),'w',encoding='utf-8') as f:
+            f.write('\\begin{tabular}{lrrrr}\\toprule\nCase & Legit accepted / total & Replay accepted & Failure mode & Request-ID \\\\\n\\midrule\n')
+            for r in rows:
+                if r.get('attempt')=='summary':f.write(f"{r['case']} & {r['legitimate_accepted']}/{r['legitimate_total']} & {r['replay_accepted']}/{r['replay_total']} & {r['nonce_fail_mode']} & {r['request_id_defense']} \\\\\n")
+            f.write('\\bottomrule\\end{tabular}\n')
+    if os.path.exists(os.path.join(E4C,'e4c.csv')):
+        rows=read(os.path.join(E4C,'e4c.csv'))
+        with open(os.path.join(E4,'retry-loss-corrected.tex'),'w',encoding='utf-8') as f:
+            f.write('\\begin{tabular}{lrrrrl}\\toprule\nCase & Loss p & Trials & Debits & Failure after debit & Retry reasons \\\\\n\\midrule\n')
+            for r in rows:
+                if r.get('kind')=='summary':f.write(f"{r['case']} & {r.get('loss_probability','')} & {r['trials']} & {r.get('debits','')} & {r.get('client_failure_after_debit','')} & \\texttt{{\\detokenize{{{r.get('client_failure_reasons','')}}}}} \\\\\n")
+                elif r.get('kind')=='insufficient-retry':f.write(f"{r['case']} & n/a & 1 & n/a & n/a & {r['initial_reason']} → {r['retry_reason']} \\\\\n")
+            f.write('\\bottomrule\\end{tabular}\n')
+print('matplotlib',matplotlib.__version__,'; wrote E1/E2/E3 figures and E1/E2/E3/E4 LaTeX tables where raw summaries exist')

+```text
+# Provisional E1 run
+
+The files in this directory are the first complete E1 protocol run. They are retained as raw evidence, but they are superseded for paper claims by `experiments/results/e1-final/`.
+
+The protocol review found that S9 used a bearer token held by the harness rather than deriving it from an attacker-visible transaction capture. The corrected runner obtains the S9 bearer from the recorded request, while the leaked signing key remains the explicitly granted S9 capability. The corrected run is stored separately so both runs remain available.
+```

+```text
+# Superseded complete E1 run
+
+These files are retained as the second completed E1 pass. It used the corrected attacker-visible S9 bearer source, but the source-review found that its money oracle queried the authenticated HTTP history endpoint rather than reading ledger rows directly from SQLite.
+
+Do not use this run for claims requiring the F1 oracle. The authoritative E1 output is `experiments/results/e1-sqlite-final/`, produced by the revised runner that performs direct SQLite queries after each scenario. No files from this superseded run have been deleted.
+```
